## 0. Conventions, standing hypotheses, and inputs used

Throughout, `k` is an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. `C` is a smooth projective connected curve of genus `g = 6` over `k`, and `gamma: C -> P^1` is a nonconstant morphism of degree four; since `C` and `P^1` are smooth curves, `gamma` is automatically finite and flat, and `C` is Gorenstein.

Write `gamma_*O_C = O_{P^1} (+) E^vee` with `E` locally free of rank three (the Tschirnhausen data), `X := P(E^vee)` with structure map `p: X -> P^1` normalized by `p_*O_X(1) = E`, and `i: C -> X` the relative-canonical (Casnati-Ekedahl) embedding.

**Standing hypotheses.**

- **(CE)** The ideal of `i` has the standard degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl resolution
  `0 -> O_X(-4) (x) p^*det F -> O_X(-2) (x) p^*F -> I_C -> 0`, with `F` locally free of rank two on `P^1`.
- **(N)** `O_X(1)|_C ~= omega_C (x) gamma^*O_{P^1}(2)`.
- **(BAL)** `F ~= O_{P^1}(4) (+) O_{P^1}(5)`.

These are exactly the hypotheses `(CE)`, `(N)`, `(BAL)` of ATT-0088 (dual-confirmed by REV-0139 and REV-0142), with `(N)` taken in the form with trivial residual twist. That normalization is legitimate: ATT-0088/CLM-0088-1 proves, from the weak form `O_X(1)|_C ~= omega_{C/P^1} (x) gamma^*A`, that `deg A = 0` and hence `A ~= O_{P^1}`. I do **not** assert `(CE)` or `(N)`; they are carried as hypotheses in Parts (A)-(D) and (F). In Part (E) they are discharged for the constructed cover by a cited source (SRC-IN-1 below), which is exactly the discharge route prescribed by packet finding FND-0150.

Set

- `D := gamma^*O_{P^1}(1)` (an effective, base-point-free divisor class of degree four),
- `W_5 := (O_X(2) (x) p^*O_{P^1}(-5))|_C` in the packet convention, and `L := W_5 (x) omega_C^{-1}`,
- `R := O_X(2)|_C`.

### 0.2 Numerology

All of the following are elementary consequences of the setup and agree with the pinned reusable computations in the working context.

- `chi(gamma_*O_C) = chi(O_C) = 1 - g = -5` and `rk(gamma_*O_C) = 4`, so `deg(gamma_*O_C) = -5 - 4 = -9`, i.e. `deg E^vee = -9` and `deg E = 9`.
- Under (N), `R = O_X(2)|_C = omega_C^{(x)2} (x) gamma^*O(4)`, so `deg R = 2*10 + 4*4 = 36`. (This reproduces `deg O_{P(E^vee)}(2)|_C = 2(2g-2+4*2) = 36`.)
- `deg W_f|_C = 2*18 - 4f = 4g + 12 - 4f`, hence `deg W_5 = 16`, `deg W_4 = 20`, and `deg L = 16 - 10 = 6`.
- `L^{(x)2} = omega_C^{(x)2}(-2D) = R (x) gamma^*O(-6)`, of degree `36 - 24 = 12 > 2g - 2 = 10`; therefore `h^1(L^{(x)2}) = 0` and `h^0(L^{(x)2}) = 12 - 6 + 1 = 7`.

## 1. The balancedness criterion

**Lemma 1.** Assume (CE) and (N). Write `gamma_*O_C = O (+) (+)_{i=1}^{3} O(-a_i)` with `a_1 <= a_2 <= a_3`, so `E = (+)_i O(a_i)` and `sum_i a_i = 9`. Then:

1. `h^0(C, gamma^*O(m)) = (m+1)_+ + sum_i (m + 1 - a_i)_+` for all `m` in `Z`.
2. `F = p_*(I_C(2))` and there is a short exact sequence `0 -> F -> Sym^2 E -> gamma_*R -> 0` on `P^1`; `F` has rank two and degree nine.
3. Fix a splitting `E = (+)_i O(a_i)` with generators `x_i`. Under (N), `gamma_*(omega_C (x) gamma^*O(2)) = O (+) E`, and the CE inclusion `E -> gamma_*(O_X(1)|_C)` is the inclusion of that summand; let `xi_i` in `H^0(C, omega_C (x) gamma^*O(2 - a_i))` be the section corresponding to `x_i`. Then the restriction map
   `res: H^0(P^1, Sym^2E(-6)) -> H^0(C, L^{(x)2})`
   sends `sum_{i<=j} c_{ij} x_i x_j` (with `c_{ij}` in `H^0(O_{P^1}(a_i + a_j - 6))`) to `sum_{i<=j} gamma^*(c_{ij}) * xi_i xi_j`, and `ker(res) = H^0(P^1, F(-6))`.
4. Writing `F ~= O(s) (+) O(9-s)` with `s <= 4`, one has `h^0(F(-6)) = 4 - s`. Consequently **(BAL) holds if and only if `res` is injective**; and if `res` fails to be injective then (BAL) fails.

*Proof.* (1) `h^0(C, gamma^*O(m)) = h^0(P^1, gamma_*O_C (x) O(m))` by finiteness of `gamma`, and the displayed formula is the sum of `h^0` over the summands.

(2) Twist the resolution (CE) by `O_X(2)`: `0 -> p^*(det F)(-2) -> p^*F -> I_C(2) -> 0`. Since `p` is a `P^2`-bundle, `R^j p_*O_X(-2) = 0` for all `j` (the only nonvanishing higher direct image of `O_X(t)` for `t < 0` occurs at `t <= -3`). Hence `p_*(p^*(det F)(-2)) = 0` and `R^1 p_*(p^*(det F)(-2)) = 0`, while `R^1 p_*(p^*F) = 0`, so `p_*(I_C(2)) = F` and `R^1 p_*(I_C(2)) = 0`. Pushing `0 -> I_C(2) -> O_X(2) -> O_C(2) -> 0` along `p` and using `p_*O_X(2) = Sym^2E`, `p_*O_C(2) = gamma_*R`, and the vanishing of `R^1p_*(I_C(2))`, gives the stated short exact sequence. Then `chi(Sym^2E) = 4*deg E + 6 = 42`, `chi(gamma_*R) = chi(R) = 36 - 6 + 1 = 31`, so `chi(F) = 11 = deg F + 2` and `deg F = 9`.

(3) By relative duality `gamma_*omega_C = Hom(gamma_*O_C, omega_{P^1}) = omega_{P^1} (+) (E (x) omega_{P^1})`, so `gamma_*(omega_C (x) gamma^*O(2)) = O (+) E`. Under (N) this is `gamma_*(O_X(1)|_C)`, and in the Casnati-Ekedahl construction the embedding `i` is the one induced by the surjection `gamma^*E -> omega_{C/P^1} = O_X(1)|_C` adjoint to the inclusion of the summand `E`. The map `Sym^2E -> gamma_*R` of (2) is `p_*` of `O_X(2) -> O_X(2)|_C`, hence on the chosen generators it is multiplication of the corresponding sections. Twisting by `O(-6)` and taking `H^0` of the left-exact sequence in (2) gives `ker(res) = H^0(F(-6))`. Note `R (x) gamma^*O(-6) = omega_C^{(x)2}(-2D) = L^{(x)2}`, so the target is `H^0(C, L^{(x)2})`, of dimension `7` by 0.2.

(4) `F(-6) = O(s-6) (+) O(3-s)` with `s <= 4`, so `h^0(F(-6)) = 0 + (4-s) = 4-s`. This vanishes exactly when `s = 4`, i.e. exactly under (BAL). Combined with `ker(res) = H^0(F(-6))` this is the stated criterion. QED

Lemma 1(4) is the engine of the whole argument, and it is the same criterion the two confirmation reviews REV-0135 and REV-0138 re-derived independently for the hyperelliptic case (`h^0(Sym^2E(-6)) = 9`, target of dimension `7`, hence `h^0(F(-6)) >= 2`). REV-0138 records explicitly that the target has `h^0 = 7` *whatever* degree-12 line bundle it is, which is the normalization-free form used there. Here I keep (N), so the target is literally `H^0(L^{(x)2})`.

## 2. Two exclusions by section count

### 2.1 Smooth plane quintics

**Lemma 2.** Let `C` be a smooth plane quintic of genus six (so `omega_C = O_C(2H)` with `H` the hyperplane class), and let `gamma: C -> P^1` be any degree-four morphism. Then, assuming (CE) and (N), `F` is not balanced.

*Proof.* *Step 1: `C` is not hyperelliptic.* `H` is special, since `h^1(H) = h^0(2H - H) = h^0(H) = 3 > 0`. On a hyperelliptic curve every special complete system is `r` copies of the `g^1_2` plus base points; with `h^0(H) = 3` this forces `r = 2` and `deg H = 5` gives a base point, contradicting very ampleness of `H`.

*Step 2: `C` is not trigonal.* Suppose `T` is a `g^1_3`; it is base-point-free (a base point would give a `g^1_2`, excluded by Step 1). The base-point-free pencil trick applied to `H^0(T) (x) H^0(H) -> H^0(T+H)` has kernel `H^0(H - T)`. If `h^0(H-T) = 0` the image has dimension at least `2*3 = 6`; but `deg(T+H) = 8`, `h^1(T+H) = h^0(2H - T - H) = h^0(H-T) = 0`, so `h^0(T+H) = 3 < 6`, a contradiction. Hence `H ~ T + q_1 + q_2` for an effective degree-two divisor. But `H` is very ample, so two points impose independent conditions on `|H|`, giving `h^0(H - q_1 - q_2) = 1`, contradicting `h^0(T) = 2`.

*Step 3: every `g^1_4` on `C` is `|H - p_0|`.* Let `D` be a `g^1_4`. It is base-point-free (a base point would give a `g^1_3`, excluded by Step 2). Apply the base-point-free pencil trick to `H^0(D) (x) H^0(H) -> H^0(D+H)`; the kernel is `H^0(H-D)`, of degree one. If `h^0(H-D) = 0`, the image has dimension at least six; but `deg(D+H) = 9`, `h^1(D+H) = h^0(H-D) = 0`, so `h^0(D+H) = 4 < 6`, a contradiction. Hence `H - D ~ p_0` for a point `p_0`, i.e. `D ~ H - p_0`.

*Step 4: the CE data.* With `D = H - p_0` one has `L = omega_C - D = 2H - H + p_0 = H + p_0`. Now `h^0(H+p_0)`: its degree is six, `chi = 1`, and `h^1(H+p_0) = h^0(2H - H - p_0) = h^0(H - p_0) = 2`, so `h^0(H+p_0) = 3 = h^0(H)`. Therefore **`p_0` is a base point of `|L|`**, and every section of `L` vanishes at `p_0`. (This reproduces the working-context established fact about the plane-quintic base point.)

Compute `E` by Lemma 1(1). First `h^0(D) = h^0(H - p_0) = 2`, so `2 = 2 + sum_i (2 - a_i)_+` forces `a_i >= 2` for all `i` (this also agrees with [V3]). Next `h^0(2D) = h^0(2H - 2p_0) = h^0(omega_C - 2p_0) = 6 - 2 = 4`, using that `2p_0` imposes two independent conditions on the canonical system precisely because `C` is not hyperelliptic. So `4 = 3 + sum_i (3-a_i)_+`, i.e. `sum_i (3-a_i)_+ = 1`. With `a_i >= 2` and `sum a_i = 9`, the only solution is `(a_1,a_2,a_3) = (2,3,4)`, i.e. `E = O(2)+O(3)+O(4)`.

*Step 5: the kernel.* `Sym^2E(-6)` has summands of degrees `-2, -1, 0, 0, 1, 2`, so `h^0(Sym^2E(-6)) = 0+0+1+1+2+3 = 7`. The section levels of Lemma 1(3) are
`xi_2` in `H^0(omega_C (x) gamma^*O(0)) = H^0(2H)`,
`xi_3` in `H^0(omega_C (x) gamma^*O(-1)) = H^0(2H - D) = H^0(H + p_0)`,
`xi_4` in `H^0(omega_C (x) gamma^*O(-2)) = H^0(2H - 2D) = H^0(2p_0)`.
Since `C` is not hyperelliptic, `h^0(2p_0) = 1` and the unique section has divisor exactly `2p_0`, so `ord_{p_0}(xi_4) = 2`. By Step 4, `ord_{p_0}(xi_3) >= 1`. Trivially `ord_{p_0}(xi_2) >= 0` and `ord_{p_0}(gamma^*c) >= 0` for any `c`.
The monomials with `a_i + a_j >= 6` are exactly `x_2x_4`, `x_3^2`, `x_3x_4`, `x_4^2` (the coefficient spaces for `x_2^2` and `x_2x_3` are `H^0(O(-2))` and `H^0(O(-1))`, both zero). Their restrictions have vanishing order at `p_0` at least `0+2 = 2`, `1+1 = 2`, `1+2 = 3`, `2+2 = 4` respectively, hence at least `2` in every case. Therefore `image(res)` is contained in `H^0(L^{(x)2}(-2p_0)) = H^0(2H + 2p_0 - 2p_0) = H^0(2H)`, of dimension six. Since the source has dimension seven, `ker(res) != 0`, so `h^0(F(-6)) >= 1` and `F` is not balanced by Lemma 1(4). QED

### 2.2 The trigonal case `L = T^{(x)2}`

**Lemma 3.** Assume (CE), (N), (BAL). Then `L` is not isomorphic to `T^{(x)2}` for a base-point-free pencil `T` of degree three.

*Proof.* Suppose `L = 2T` with `t: C -> P^1` the degree-three morphism attached to `T`. By [V2], `C` is not hyperelliptic; by [V3], `h^0(L) = 3` and `h^0(O_C(D)) = 2` with `D = gamma^*O(1)` base-point-free of degree four. Since `t^*: H^0(P^1, O(2)) -> H^0(2T)` is injective between spaces of dimension three, it is an isomorphism:

  **(*) `H^0(L) = H^0(2T) = t^*H^0(P^1, O_{P^1}(2))`**, so every divisor of `|2T|` is `t^*(e)` for a unique `e` in `|O_{P^1}(2)|`.

*Step 1: `h^0(4T - omega_C) = 0`.* Note `4T - omega_C = 2L - omega_C = omega_C - 2D` has degree `2`. Since `C` is not hyperelliptic, `h^0` of a degree-two bundle is at most one. Suppose `h^0(4T - omega_C) = 1`, so `4T ~ omega_C + A` with `A >= 0` of degree two. Then `D = omega_C - 2T ~ 2T - A`, and by (*),
`|D| = { t^*(e) - A : e in |O(2)|, t^*(e) >= A }`.
Write `A = a_1 + a_2` (possibly `a_1 = a_2`).
 - If `t(a_1) != t(a_2)`: then `e` must contain both points, so `e` is unique and `h^0(D) = 1`, contradicting `h^0(D) = 2`.
 - If `a_1 != a_2` and `t(a_1) = t(a_2) = s`: then `t^*(e) >= A` iff `e >= s`, so `|D| = (t^*(s) - A) + |T|` and `t^*(s) - A` is a single point `p_0`, which is then a base point of `|D|`, contradicting base-point-freeness of `D`.
 - If `a_1 = a_2 = a`, `s = t(a)`: if `t` is unramified at `a`, then `t^*(e) >= 2a` forces `e >= 2s`, so `e` is unique and `h^0(D) = 1`, a contradiction; if `t` is ramified at `a`, then `e >= s` suffices, `|D| = (t^*(s) - 2a) + |T|`, and `t^*(s) - 2a` is a single point, again a base point of `|D|`, a contradiction.
All cases are impossible, so `h^0(4T - omega_C) = 0`.

*Step 2: `E = O(3)^{(+)3}`.* By Lemma 1(1) and `h^0(D) = 2` we get `a_i >= 2` for all `i` (also [V3]). Next `h^0(2D) = chi(2D) + h^1(2D) = (8 - 6 + 1) + h^0(omega_C - 2D) = 3 + h^0(4T - omega_C) = 3` by Step 1. So `3 = 3 + sum_i (3 - a_i)_+`, forcing `a_i >= 3` for all `i`; with `sum a_i = 9` this gives `a_i = 3` for all `i`.

*Step 3: the kernel.* `Sym^2E(-6) = O^{(+)6}`, so `h^0(Sym^2E(-6)) = 6` and every coefficient `c_{ij}` lies in `H^0(O(0))`, i.e. is a constant. Also `E(-3) = O^{(+)3}` sits inside `gamma_*(omega_C (x) gamma^*O(-1)) = gamma_*L`, and `h^0(E(-3)) = 3 = h^0(L)`, so the three sections `xi_i` form a basis of `H^0(L)`. Consequently `res` is exactly the multiplication map
`Sym^2 H^0(L) -> H^0(L^{(x)2})`.
By (*), `H^0(L) = t^*H^0(O_{P^1}(2))`, hence the image of `res` lies in `t^*H^0(O_{P^1}(4))`, which has dimension five (as `t^*` is injective). The source has dimension six, so `ker(res) != 0`, `h^0(F(-6)) >= 1`, and `F` is not balanced by Lemma 1(4). This contradicts (BAL). QED

*Remark.* The same conclusion is reached with no use of the Maroni/Hirzebruch classification of trigonal curves. Note also that `E = O(3)^{(+)3}` by itself is compatible with balancedness (the working context records a `(1,2)`-`(2,2)` complete intersection in `P^1 x P^2` with `E^vee = O(-3)^3` and `F = O(4)+O(5)`); what is incompatible is `E = O(3)^3` *together with* `H^0(L)` being a pullback along a degree-three map. So the exclusion is genuinely about `L = 2T`, not about the splitting type of `E`.

## 3. Part (A): `L` is base-point-free

**Proposition 4.** Assume (CE), (N), (BAL). Then `L` is base-point-free.

*Proof.* By [V3] and [V6], `h^0(L) = 3` on every balanced fibre. Suppose `p` is a base point, i.e. `h^0(L(-p)) = 3`. Since `L = omega_C - D`, we have `L(-p) = omega_C - (D+p)`, and `chi(D+p) = 5 - 6 + 1 = 0`, so by Riemann-Roch and Serre duality `h^0(D+p) = h^1(D+p) = h^0(omega_C - D - p) = h^0(L(-p)) = 3`. Thus `|D+p|` is a `g^2_5`.

- If `|D+p|` has a base point `q`, then `|D + p - q|` is a `g^2_4`, so `h^0 = 3 = deg/2 + 1`, i.e. equality in Clifford's theorem, with `deg = 4` not in `{0, 2g-2} = {0,10}`. Clifford equality then forces `C` hyperelliptic, contradicting [V2].
- If `|D+p|` is base-point-free, it defines a finite morphism `phi: C -> P^2` with nondegenerate image `X'` (the system is complete of projective dimension two), and `deg(phi) * deg(X') = 5`. Nondegeneracy gives `deg X' >= 2`, so `deg phi = 1` and `deg X' = 5`. Then `X'` is an irreducible plane quintic whose normalization is `C` of genus six; since the arithmetic genus of a plane quintic is `(5-1)(5-2)/2 = 6`, the delta invariant is zero and `X'` is smooth, so `C` is a smooth plane quintic. By Lemma 2 this contradicts (BAL).

Both branches are impossible, so `L` has no base point. QED

Since `L` is base-point-free of degree six with `h^0(L) = 3`, the morphism `phi_L: C -> P^2 = P(H^0(L)^vee)` is finite (it is nonconstant, and `C` is a curve) onto an irreducible curve `X_L` which is nondegenerate because the system is complete; and `deg(phi_L) * deg(X_L) = deg L = 6`. This is Part (A). Under the identification of `|L|` with the dual plane `(P^2)^vee`, the members of `|L|` are exactly the pullbacks `phi_L^*(l)` of lines `l`.

*Comparison with the dependency.* ATT-0088/CLM-0088-4 proves only that the fixed part of `|L|` has degree at most one and the moving part is base-point-free of degree **five or six**, and REV-0142 records explicitly that "No claim is made that `L` itself is base-point-free"; ATT-0088's `theorem_scope.not_covered` lists base-point-freeness as "neither asserted nor denied". Proposition 4 removes the degree-five alternative. (Packet finding FND-0134 asserts the same conclusion by the same plane-quintic route; the point of Lemma 2 and Proposition 4 is to supply the proof, including the missing step that every `g^1_4` on a plane quintic is `|H-p_0|`.)

## 4. Part (B): the dichotomy

**Proposition 5.** Assume (CE), (N), (BAL). Then either `deg phi_L = 1` (type (i)) or `deg phi_L = 2` with `X_L` a smooth plane cubic and `gamma` bielliptic-composed as in the theorem statement (type (ii)).

*Proof.* `deg phi_L` divides `6` and `deg X_L = 6/deg phi_L >= 2`.

- `deg phi_L = 6` would give `deg X_L = 1`, contradicting nondegeneracy.
- `deg phi_L = 3` gives `deg X_L = 2`; an irreducible nondegenerate plane conic is smooth, hence isomorphic to `P^1`. So `t := (C -> X_L ~= P^1)` is a degree-three morphism, and `L = phi_L^*O_{P^2}(1) = t^*(O_{P^1}(2)) = 2T` with `T := t^*O_{P^1}(1)` a base-point-free `g^1_3`. This is excluded by Lemma 3.
- `deg phi_L = 2` gives `deg X_L = 3`. Suppose `X_L` were singular. Then its normalization is `P^1` (an irreducible singular plane cubic has geometric genus zero), and since `C` is smooth, `phi_L` factors through the normalization, giving a degree-two morphism `h: C -> P^1`, i.e. `C` hyperelliptic, contradicting [V2]. (Alternatively and independently: then `L = h^*O_{P^1}(3)` would have `h^0 >= 4 > 3`.) ## 5. Part (C): full `S_6` monodromy in type (i)

**Lemma 8 (2-transitivity).** `G` is 2-transitive.

**Lemma 9 (a transposition).** `G` contains a transposition.

In particular Part (C) is a statement about a geometric monodromy image only: by FND-0053, FND-0085 and FND-0152(ii) it upgrades nothing to Tate type, and the `H_alpha`-object `F(Z_alpha^1)` of FND-0152 remains a separate geometric and Hodge input. What Part (C) does supply downstream is that for type-(i) components the induction in FND-0152 is trivial, so `F(Z_alpha) = F(U_alpha)`-computations need no coset bookkeeping.

## 10. Consistency checks against the recorded corpus

- `E = O(2)+O(3)+O(4)` in the plane-quintic case reproduces the working-context established facts `Sym^2E(-6) ~= O(-2)+O(-1)+O(0)^2+O(1)+O(2)` with `h^0 = 7`, and `h^0(2H+2p) = 7` with the six-dimensional subspace `H^0(2H)`; the recorded base-point statement `L = H+p` with `p` a base point is exactly Step 4 of Lemma 2.
- The bielliptic-composed case has `h^0(O_C(D)) = 2` and `h^0(L) = 3`, consistent with [V3], [V6] and FND-0142, and `C` is not hyperelliptic (Castelnuovo-Severi: a degree-two map to `P^1` and a degree-two map to `Y` would need a common degree-two factor, forcing `P^1 ~= Y`), consistent with [V2].
- `E = O(3)^{(+)3}` occurs both in the excluded trigonal case and in the balanced `(1,2)`-`(2,2)` complete intersection in `P^1 x P^2` recorded as a reusable computation; there is no conflict, since `F` is not determined by `E`, and the trigonal exclusion turns on `H^0(L)` being a pullback along a degree-three map. The complete-intersection example is type (i) and is not used as an input.
- Poincare-duality bookkeeping for the campaign target (`d = 3*6-3+6 = 21`, `2d-16 = 26`, `Q(-13)(21) = Q(8)`) is untouched by this lemma, which makes no cohomological claim.

claims.statement: Assume (CE) and (N). With gamma_*O_C = O + (+)_i O(-a_i), E = (+)_i O(a_i), sum a_i = 9, one has F = p_*(I_C(2)), an exact sequence 0 -> F -> Sym^2E -> gamma_*R -> 0 with F of rank two and degree nine, and ker(H^0(Sym^2E(-6)) -> H^0(C, L^{tensor 2})) = H^0(F(-6)). Writing F = O(s)+O(9-s) with s <= 4, h^0(F(-6)) = 4-s; hence (BAL) holds if and only if that restriction map is injective. The target H^0(C, L^{tensor 2}) always has dimension seven.

On a smooth plane quintic of genus six every g^1_4 is |H - p_0| for a point p_0; consequently L = H + p_0 has p_0 as a base point, E = O(2)+O(3)+O(4), and the restriction map of CLM-0103-1 has seven-dimensional source but image inside the six-dimensional H^0(omega_C), so h^0(F(-6)) >= 1. Hence no degree-four pencil on a smooth plane quintic has balanced CE relations bundle.
Under (CE)+(N)+(BAL), L is base-point-free. Equivalently, the fixed part of |L| left open by ATT-0088/CLM-0088-4 (degree zero or one) has degree zero.

Under (CE)+(N)+(BAL), L is not isomorphic to T^{tensor 2} for any base-point-free degree-three pencil T. The proof shows h^0(4T - omega_C) = 0 (otherwise D = omega_C - 2T acquires a base point, contradicting D = gamma^*O(1)), whence E = O(3)^3, the restriction map is the multiplication Sym^2 H^0(L) -> H^0(L^{tensor 2}) whose image lies in the five-dimensional t^*H^0(O_{P^1}(4)), and h^0(F(-6)) >= 1.

Under (CE)+(N)+(BAL), phi_L : C -> P^2 is finite onto an irreducible nondegenerate plane curve and exactly one of the following holds: deg phi_L = 1 with image a plane sextic of geometric genus six (type (i)); or deg phi_L = 2 with image a smooth plane cubic Y, phi_L = psi a bielliptic double cover, omega_C = psi^*M with deg M = 5, L = psi^*N with deg N = 3, gamma = q o psi with q = phi_{|M tensor N^{-1}|} of degree two, and E = O(2)+O(3)+O(4) (type (ii)). Degrees 3 and 6, singular cubic images, hyperelliptic C and smooth plane quintic C do not occur.

In type (i), the geometric monodromy image of pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs}) -> S_6 acting on the six points of a general divisor of |L| is the full symmetric group S_6, and the finite etale S_6-torsor Ord(|L|^{rs}) is connected. The proof uses irreducibility of the point-line incidence (transitivity), irreducibility of the ordered-pair incidence (2-transitivity, using birationality of phi_L), a simple tangent line at a general point of the dual curve (a transposition, using characteristic-zero reflexivity and finiteness of the inflection divisor), and Jordan's theorem.

In type (ii), the fibres of psi induce a monodromy-invariant partition of each reduced divisor of |L| into three blocks of size two; hence the fibrewise geometric monodromy image is contained in the imprimitive wreath subgroup S_2 wr S_3 of order 48 and is not S_6.

Type (ii) is nonempty: for every elliptic Y, every P in Pic^2(Y) with associated degree-two q, every M in Pic^5(Y) whose unique point y_0 with O(y_0) = M tensor P^{-2} avoids the four ramification points of q, and every reduced B in |M^{tensor 2}|, the double cover psi : C -> Y branched along B is a smooth connected genus-six curve and gamma = q o psi is a finite flat degree-four cover satisfying (BAL). Hence a non-primitive degree-four pencil factoring through an intermediate curve of genus one can have balanced Casnati-Ekedahl splitting, and primitivity of gamma is not a property of the balanced locus.

Over a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme S carrying a balanced (CE)+(N) genus-six degree-four family, with U the reduced-support open of AJ = P_S(pi_*L) and Z = Ord(U) the S_6-torsor of ATT-0088/CLM-0088-8: for every connected component S_alpha over which at least one geometric fibre is of type (i), the geometric monodromy image H_alpha equals S_6 and Z_alpha is connected; if moreover U_alpha is normal, integral and locally Noetherian then Z_alpha is irreducible, [S_6 : H_alpha] = 1, and the FND-0152 induction functor is the identity. No irreducibility hypothesis on S or on the balanced base is used.

gap_markers.statement: The exact monodromy image in type (ii) is not determined; only containment in S_2 wr S_3 is proved. Determining whether it equals the full wreath product (and hence computing the isotypic decomposition on the type-(ii) locus) is left open.

It is not determined whether a connected component of the balanced base can consist entirely of type-(ii) fibres, i.e. whether the type-(i) hypothesis in Part (F) is automatic. This is a question about the dimension and closure of the bielliptic-composed sublocus inside the balanced base, and it interacts with the still-open frontier obligation on irreducibility of that base. Part (F) is stated conditionally on the hypothesis and does not assume it away.

gap_markers.statement: Non-primitive degree-four pencils factoring through intermediate curves of genus two or three are not analyzed. Only intermediate genus zero (excluded, via ATT-0088/CLM-0088-2 and FND-0125) and intermediate genus one (realized, Part (E)) are settled. Note that in the dichotomy of Part (B) such covers, if balanced, would have to be of type (i), since their phi_L cannot factor through the intermediate curve by degree reasons; so this gap does not affect (A)-(D) or (F).

Part (F) is stated over reduced locally Noetherian schemes, matching ATT-0088 Part III. The extension to algebraic stacks with a smooth atlas (the one-line descent recorded as FND-0127) and to nonreduced bases (where Grauert fails, FND-0131) is not carried out here.

Hypotheses (CE) and (N) are carried as explicit hypotheses in Parts (A)-(D) and (F) and are discharged in Part (E) only by the source-backed input SRC-IN-1 (Casnati-Ekedahl 1996 Theorem 2.1 and SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6). No independent construction of the CE embedding or resolution is given here.

Lemma 9 invokes two classical characteristic-zero inputs that are not reproved: reflexivity/biduality for reduced irreducible plane curves (birationality of the Gauss map onto the dual curve) and Jordan's theorem on primitive groups containing a transposition.

novelty_claims.statement: Base-point-freeness of L on the balanced locus is proved. ATT-0088/CLM-0088-4 established only that the fixed part of |L| has degree at most one, and REV-0142 records explicitly that no claim is made that L itself is base-point-free; ATT-0088 theorem_scope lists this as neither asserted nor denied. The missing ingredient supplied here is the classification of g^1_4's on a smooth plane quintic together with an explicit vanishing-order computation excluding balancedness there.

A complete dichotomy for the degree-six morphism phi_L on the balanced locus: it is either birational onto a plane sextic or exactly two-to-one onto a smooth plane cubic with gamma bielliptic-composed. This includes a new exclusion of the trigonal possibility L = T^{tensor 2}, obtained without the Maroni/Hirzebruch classification of trigonal curves.

First determination of a geometric monodromy image for the finite etale S_6-cover of the C66-GEO-COMP frontier: the fibrewise monodromy is the full S_6 in type (i). This addresses the recorded frontier obligation that neither fullness of S_6, nor the existence of a transposition, nor the occurrence loci were established; both fullness and an explicit transposition (local monodromy at a general point of the dual sextic) are now proved, and the occurrence locus is identified as exactly the type-(i) locus.

Affirmative resolution, for intermediate genus one, of the frontier obligation on whether a non-primitive degree-four pencil factoring through a positive-genus intermediate curve can have balanced CE splitting. The construction is universal in (Y,P,M,B) rather than a single model, and its balancedness proof uses only the Lemma-1 criterion, not any criterion of ATT-0100, so it complies with FND-0150.

A component-local family statement (Part (F)) that yields H_alpha = S_6 from a single geometric fibre and therefore requires no irreducibility hypothesis on the balanced base, sidestepping the still-open frontier obligation on base irreducibility.

parsed_artifact.summary: Determines the finite-cover behaviour of the ordered S_6-torsor over the balanced tetragonal CE geometry at (g,n)=(6,6), and settles two of the recorded frontier obligations. Working on a single balanced geometric fibre under (CE)+(N)+(BAL), the residual bundle L = omega_C(-D) is shown to be base-point-free (a point ATT-0088/REV-0142 explicitly leave open), and the associated degree-six morphism phi_L: C -> P^2 is shown to be either birational onto a plane sextic (type (i)) or exactly two-to-one onto a smooth plane cubic, in which case gamma is bielliptic-composed (type (ii)). The intermediate possibilities are eliminated: hyperelliptic fibres by the confirmed CLM-0088-2, smooth plane quintics and the trigonal case L = T^{tensor 2} by two new section-count computations of the same kind as the confirmed hyperelliptic obstruction. In type (i) the fibrewise geometric monodromy of the S_6-ordering torsor is proved to be the full symmetric group, by combining transitivity and two-transitivity of the incidence varieties with a transposition supplied by a general tangent line and Jordan's theorem; this is the first determination of a monodromy image for this cover and it needs no irreducibility hypothesis on the balanced base. In type (ii) the monodromy is imprimitive, contained in S_2 wr S_3. Type (ii) is then shown to be nonempty by an explicit but universal construction: for every elliptic Y, every P in Pic^2(Y) and every M in Pic^5(Y) whose associated point y_0 avoids the four ramification points of q = phi_{|P|}, the double cover of Y branched along a reduced member of |M^{tensor 2}| is a smooth genus-six curve whose composed degree-four pencil is balanced. Hence a non-primitive degree-four pencil through a positive-genus intermediate curve can have balanced CE splitting, answering the corresponding frontier obligation affirmatively for intermediate genus one, and showing that primitivity of gamma is not available on the balanced locus. The family consequence is stated component-locally: over any connected component of a reduced base meeting the type-(i) locus, the monodromy image is S_6, the ordering torsor is connected, and (under normality) irreducible, so the FND-0152 induction is trivial. No Tate-type conclusion is drawn.

theorem_scope.base: Parts (A)-(E) are statements about a single geometric point, i.e. a pair (C,gamma) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. parsed_artifact.theorem_statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, C a smooth projective connected curve of genus 6 over k, and gamma: C -> P^1 a finite flat morphism of degree four, with gamma_*O_C = O_{P^1} + E^vee (E of rank three and degree nine), Casnati-Ekedahl embedding i: C -> X = P(E^vee), p: X -> P^1, p_*O_X(1) = E. Assume (CE) the ideal of i has the standard degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl resolution 0 -> O_X(-4) tensor p^*det F -> O_X(-2) tensor p^*F -> I_C -> 0 with F of rank two; (N) O_X(1)|_C is isomorphic to omega_C tensor gamma^*O_{P^1}(2); and (BAL) F is isomorphic to O_{P^1}(4) + O_{P^1}(5). Put D = gamma^*O_{P^1}(1) and L = W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} = omega_C(-D), of degree six with h^0(L) = 3. THEN: (A) L is base-point-free, so phi_L: C -> P^2 is a finite morphism onto an irreducible nondegenerate plane curve X_L with deg(phi_L)*deg(X_L) = 6. (B) Exactly one of two cases holds. Case (i): deg(phi_L) = 1 and X_L is a plane sextic with normalization C. Case (ii): deg(phi_L) = 2 and X_L is a smooth plane cubic; writing Y = X_L and psi = phi_L: C -> Y, the curve Y is elliptic, psi is a bielliptic double cover with psi_*O_C = O_Y + M^{-1}, deg M = 5, omega_C = psi^*M, L = psi^*N with N = O_{X_L}(1) of degree three, E is isomorphic to O(2)+O(3)+O(4), and gamma = q o psi where q = phi_{|P|}: Y -> P^1 is the degree-two morphism attached to P = M tensor N^{-1} in Pic^2(Y); in particular gamma is non-primitive and factors through a curve of genus one. The remaining possibilities do not occur: deg(phi_L) is never 3 or 6, X_L is never a singular cubic, C is never hyperelliptic and never a smooth plane quintic, and L is never the square of a base-point-free degree-three pencil. (C) In case (i), let |L|^{rs} be the open subset of |L| = P^2 of divisors with six pairwise-distinct points and Ord(|L|^{rs}) -> |L|^{rs} the finite etale right S_6-torsor of orderings. Then Ord(|L|^{rs}) is connected and the geometric monodromy image of pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs}) -> S_6 is the full symmetric group S_6. (D) In case (ii), the fibres of psi cut each divisor of |L|^{rs} into three blocks of size two, and this partition is monodromy-invariant; hence the monodromy image lies in the imprimitive wreath subgroup S_2 wr S_3 of order 48 and is not S_6. (E) Case (ii) is nonempty. Let Y be an elliptic curve over k, P in Pic^2(Y) with degree-two morphism q = phi_{|P|}: Y -> P^1, M in Pic^5(Y) such that the unique point y_0 with O_Y(y_0) isomorphic to M tensor P^{-2} is not a ramification point of q, and B in |M^{tensor 2}| reduced; let psi: C -> Y be the double cover branched along B. Then C is smooth connected of genus six, gamma = q o psi is finite flat of degree four, and (C,gamma) satisfies (BAL). Such data exist, and (CE) and (N) hold for every such (C,gamma) by the source-backed input SRC-IN-1. Hence the balanced locus contains tetragonal pencils factoring through a genus-one intermediate curve. (F) Let S be a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme carrying a genus-six degree-four family satisfying (CE), (BAL) and (N) on every geometric fibre, AJ = P_S(pi_*L), U the reduced-support open of AJ, and Z = Ord(U) -> U the finite etale S_6-torsor of orderings of ATT-0088 (III). If S_alpha is a connected component of S over which some geometric fibre is of type (i), then the geometric monodromy image H_alpha of pi_1^{et}(U_alpha) -> S_6 equals S_6; consequently Z_alpha is connected, and if U_alpha is in addition normal, integral and locally Noetherian then Z_alpha is irreducible, the component index [S_6 : H_alpha] equals one, and the S_6-induction functor of FND-0152 is the identity. No Hodge, weight or Tate conclusion is asserted anywhere in (A)-(F).
